source.title: InterPLM: Discovering Interpretable Features in Protein Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figures and table layouts are flattened, but the relevant neuron and feature counts are also stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares individual ESM-2 neurons with SAE features using Swiss-Prot concept associations, a different measure of interpretability from the claimed audit of neuron-pole job shares.
record.gate_note: The text reports neuron-to-concept associations and a comparison with SAE features, so these results bear on neuron interpretability. It does not report the claimed proportions of poles with one job, two related jobs, or unknown jobs. The LLM-generated description result concerns SAE features, not explanations of neurons.
record.test_reason: The paper measures how many individual ESM-2-8M units align with known biological concepts and compares them with SAE features. This bears weakly on V2 (neuron interpretability in another, small, dense language model). Caveat: the 'neurons' are the 320 residual-stream dimensions after each transformer block, not MLP neurons or poles. Interpretability is scored only against 433 Swiss-Prot concepts.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that ESM-2 neurons are polysemantic and that the gap of 46 vs 2,548 concept-aligned units per layer is strong evidence of superposition. They add that SAE features give a more interpretable, quantitatively evaluable framework, and that shuffled-weight models yield no biological-concept features.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Swiss-Prot concept associations and F1-based evaluation in ESM-2-8M, rather than auditing explanations of positive and negative neuron poles in Qwen3-32B.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected SAE models and reported counts depend on layer-wise model selection using Swiss-Prot concept associations; the paper reports the maxima across layers in its prose.

fits_no_version.finding: SAE features align with far more Swiss-Prot concepts than ESM-2 units do: up to 2,548 vs 46 per layer, and 143 vs 15 concepts. Shuffled-weight SAEs yield zero concept features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a small protein language model, SAE features recover many more known concepts than residual-stream units, which the authors read as superposition.

fits_no_version.finding: Claude-3.5 Sonnet descriptions of 1,200 SAE features predict maximum activations on held-out proteins with median Pearson r = 0.72.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM-generated descriptions of protein-model SAE features predict activation levels on new proteins moderately well.

record.problems: The study evaluates neuron interpretability through Swiss-Prot concept associations rather than direct human judgments of neuron jobs or a pole-level audit. The reported neuron and SAE counts are maxima across layers, and the text does not give uncertainty estimates for them.
record.rows_left_out: No further claim-relevant results were reported separately in the text. The LLM feature-description evaluation is included as r4 but is not linked to the neuron-explanation versions.

untested.parts: All: no Qwen3-32B, no pole-level audit, no shares of units with one, two or unknown jobs.
Mixture-of-experts and large models (only 8M dense); MLP neurons or poles; a full audit of what each unit does beyond the Swiss-Prot concept list.
All: simulation scoring is applied only to SAE features, not neurons.

missing.what: Per-layer counts of neurons with concept F1>0.5 (only the maximum of 46 is in the text)
Percent of neurons per layer with F1>0.5 to an individual amino-acid type. This is a simpler kind of job that could raise the share of interpretable units.
Per-concept best-neuron held-out F1 compared with SAE features

record.verdict_notes: The units called 'neurons' are hidden-state dimensions after each transformer block, i.e. the residual stream, which has no privileged basis. They are not the MLP neurons or poles the essay audits. Interpretability is judged only by matching a fixed annotation set, so units with jobs outside Swiss-Prot count as uninterpretable. Even SAE features are under 20% labeled by Swiss-Prot. The tranche is T3 rather than T2 because this is a new model domain with a different construct. The record's 10,420 dictionary size conflicts with the 10,240 stated in Methods.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B, distinguish positive and negative neuron poles, or estimate the shares with one main job, two related jobs, or unresolved jobs.
Tests ESM-2-8M only; does not compare dense and mixture-of-experts models, test very large models, or estimate the claimed pole-job shares.
Does not analyze InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not test architecture or regularization effects, vision models, or the claimed change in interpretability estimates with tools.
Does not test whether attribution graphs built from a large model's own neurons explain its behaviour.
Does not test neuron explanations against the neurons' firing on new text; its held-out activation prediction concerns SAE features in a protein model.
Does not score explanations of neurons by simulating their activations on new text.

rows.measure: Number of neurons with clear concept associations and number of distinct associated concepts
rows.value: At most 46 neurons per layer with clear conceptual alignment across 15 known concepts
rows.note: The text reports the maximum across layers, not layer-specific counts. This measure does not directly estimate the proportion of neuron poles with a particular number of jobs.
rows.check: Remove V1: Qwen3-32B is not studied. The units are residual-stream embedding dimensions (320 per layer), not MLP neurons, and poles are not separated. The value is a per-layer maximum of 46 of 320 units (~14%) with F1>0.5 to a Swiss-Prot concept, covering 15 concepts. This is a lower bound limited by annotation coverage, not a share of units with one job. Baseline should read 'shuffled-weight model / SAE comparison', not 'not stated'.

source_check.correct: State for V2 should be cannot_determine. The measure is residual-stream dimensions with F1>0.5 to one of 433 Swiss-Prot concepts, and it cannot show a one-main-job share. Under the same metric even SAE features reach at most 2,548 of 10,240 per layer (~25%), so a unit with a clear job outside the annotations is not counted. 46 of 320 is a per-layer maximum.
source_check.locator_found: Abstract; Sec 3.3 (46 vs 2,548; 15 vs 143 concepts); Methods 5.1.2 (dictionary 10,240 from 320-dim embeddings), 5.2.4 (neurons via identity SAE); Fig 9b (neuron-amino-acid associations counted separately)
source_check.problem: Concept-annotation F1 on residual-stream dims is a lower bound limited by coverage, so it cannot show the V2 effect. Partial overstates it.

relationships.condition: ESM-2-8M residual-stream units scored against 433 Swiss-Prot concepts (F1>0.5 on validation and test)
relationships.reason: At most 46/320 units per layer (~14%) match a known concept, covering 15 concepts, versus up to 2,548 SAE features (r1). Matching is limited by annotation coverage, so this is weak, indirect evidence below the ~90% share.
relationships.display_finding: At most 46 of 320 units per layer (about 14%) matched a known concept, covering 15 concepts in total, against up to 2,548 SAE features. Matching depends on which concepts are annotated, so this is weak, indirect evidence.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: ESM-2-8M residual-stream units scored against 433 Swiss-Prot concepts (F1>0.5 on validation and test)
labels.reason: r1 cannot show a one-job share. Matching is limited to 433 annotated concepts (SAE features reach only ~25% on it), the units are residual-stream dims, and poles and job counts are not measured. This makes V2 untested here, not limits_scope.

relation.reason: Its results cannot show whether V2 holds (row cannot_determine, verdict none). The paper discusses neuron polysemanticity and superposition, inferring it from the neuron vs SAE gap.

tranche.reason: The study measures a related but different construct: concept-annotation F1 of residual-stream dims, a lower bound that even SAE features score ~25% on. It cannot bear on V2's one-job share, and no other version is tested. It neither tests nor uses the finding.

source_check.notes: The 'neurons' are the 320 residual-stream dimensions after each of the 6 blocks of ESM-2-8M, not MLP neurons. Neurons aligned with amino-acid identity (Fig 9b) are excluded from the 46. Sec 3.1 says 10,420 features but Methods gives 10,240 (32x320). The authors_conclusion paraphrase is correct.

statements.correction: ESM-2-8M, residual-stream dims (320 per layer): at most 46 per layer have F1>0.5 with one of 433 Swiss-Prot concepts on both validation and test. That is 15 distinct concepts with neurons vs 143 with SAE features. SAE features reach up to 2,548 of 10,240 per layer (~25%) on the same metric. There is no pole split and no job count. Verdict for V2: none (untested), so the study should not be listed in V2.against.
statements.problem: The ESM-2 numbers are in the text (46, 320, 15, 2,548, 433; 14% is marked as derived). But the study is filed as limits_scope evidence against V2, and its metric cannot show one-job shares: even SAE features reach only ~25% under it. The study does not test V2.
Correct for this study. The units are 320-dim hidden representations after each transformer block (residual-stream dimensions), and no two-related-jobs share is reported.

statements.correction: ESM-2-8M is a protein language model (ESM-2-8M-UR50D, trained on UniRef50). Its r1 measure (Swiss-Prot concept F1 on residual-stream dims) cannot show V2's share, so the study does not test V2. Only pi0.5 would remain as a non-text model tested against V2.
statements.problem: ESM-2-8M is correctly called a protein language model. But the statement counts it among 'the models tested against V2', and on this check the study does not test V2: its row r1 is cannot_determine and its verdict is none.

statements.correction: SAE counts: one SAE per layer, selected from 20 by mean top-F1 on 20% of validation. Neuron counts: neuron values scaled 0-1 and passed through a 1x identity SAE, with no model selection. The text reports maxima (46 neurons, 2,548 SAE features per layer) and says the gap 'persisted across model layers'. Per-layer counts are only in Figure 3b.
statements.problem: 46 is the per-layer maximum, which is correct. But 'counts come from layer-wise model selection' holds only for the SAE counts: one SAE per layer chosen from 20. The neuron counts use an identity-matrix SAE with no model selection. The text gives no per-layer neuron counts in prose.
